listening.en: When the coordinator left for her afternoon class, Arun took over the sign-in desk, handling arrivals and recording messages until she returned.
listening.zh: 協調員去上下午課時，阿倫接手登記處，處理抵達及記留言，直到她回來。
listening.promptZh: 阿倫接手了甚麼範圍？

options.en: Responsibility for the sign-in desk during the coordinator’s absence.
options.zh: 協調員離開期間的登記處責任。

options.en: Permanent management of the whole organisation.
options.zh: 整個機構的永久管理。

options.en: Only observing the coordinator while she continued to handle arrivals.
options.zh: 只在旁看協調員，而抵達者仍由她處理。

options.en: The coordinator’s teaching duties at her afternoon class.
options.zh: 協調員下午課的教學責任。

listening.explanationZh: desk及until returned 給範圍與時限，沒有全機構或教學。

reply.promptZh: 協調員去上課時，阿倫做了甚麼？
reply.promptEn: What did Arun do while the coordinator went to class?

options.en: He handled arrivals and messages at the desk until she came back.
options.zh: 他在登記處處理抵達及留言，直到她回來。

options.en: He took over the sign-in desk during her afternoon class.
options.zh: 她上下午課期間，他接手登記處。

options.en: He became the person responsible for the desk while she was away.
options.zh: 她離開時，他成為登記處的負責人。

options.en: He covered the desk’s work temporarily rather than merely watching it.
options.zh: 他暫代登記處工作，不只在旁看。

reply.explanationZh: 四句都描述暫時接責，沒有加永久任命。

scene.promptZh: 原主持需離開十分鐘，你獲交名單及流程，在其間點名、安排下一位發言，待她回來交還。哪句準確？

options.en: I took over the chairing duties for ten minutes.
options.zh: 我接手主持責任十分鐘。

options.en: I watched the original chair continue leading every turn.
options.zh: 我看着原主持繼續帶領每次發言。

options.en: I was appointed permanent head of the whole club.
options.zh: 我獲任命為整個社團的永久主管。

scene.explanationZh: 交流程並執行主持是暫時接手，不是旁觀或永久升任。

contrast.promptZh: 哪項最不足以支持 took over the task？

options.en: The new person became responsible for carrying out the task.
options.zh: 新的人負責執行該任務。

options.en: The new person only offered one suggestion while the original person kept full responsibility.
options.zh: 新人只提一個建議，全部責任仍由原人承擔。

options.en: Responsibility transferred for an agreed period.
options.zh: 責任轉交一段議定時間。

contrast.explanationZh: 給建議不等於接責，需看實際分工。

dialogue.promptZh: 同伴把阿倫暫代登記處，寫成協調員被撤職；她只是去上課並會回來。哪句修訂準確？

options.en: Describe the temporary cover and its end point without inventing a dismissal.
options.zh: 描述暫代及結束時點，不編撤職。

options.en: Treat a short handover as confirmation that the coordinator lost her position.
options.zh: 把短交接當協調員失去職位的確認。

options.en: Remove Arun’s responsibility because temporary cover cannot count as taking over.
options.zh: 因暫代不算接手，就刪阿倫的責任。

dialogue.explanationZh: 接手可暫時，不能推撤職，也不因有時限就否定責任。

speaking.en: I took over the task for the afternoon and handed it back when the coordinator returned.
speaking.zh: 我下午接手任務，協調員回來時再交還。
speaking.promptZh: 先聽，再說清接手及交還。

writing.promptZh: 新情境：你們一起編家庭口述史，哥哥已訪問祖父，但接下來一周沒空；你接手把現有錄音整理成逐字稿，不代他增加新訪問或更改祖父原意。用一至兩句英文說明接手範圍及核對安排。
writing.selfCheckZh: 交代接的是已有錄音逐字稿、何時暫代及疑詞核對，不加新訪問責任或擅改原話。

examples.en: I will take over the transcription of the existing recordings while my brother is busy this week. We will check any unclear words together afterwards.
examples.zh: 哥哥這周忙，我會接手把現有錄音整理成逐字稿。之後我們會一起核對聽不清的字。

examples.en: My brother has handed me the recordings, so I am taking over the transcript rather than planning new interviews. I will mark uncertain words for review.
examples.zh: 哥哥已把錄音交給我，所以我接手逐字稿，不是安排新訪問。我會標記不確定的字待核對。

takeaways.en: She took over the final checks while her colleague prepared the handover notes.
takeaways.zh: 同事準備交接筆記時，她接手最後核對。

takeaways.en: We need to know who will take over the booking task during the holiday.
takeaways.zh: 我們需知道假期由誰接手預約任務。

brief.meaningEn: Leave a lasting impression or influence; a deeper footprint compares stronger impact, while the same deep footprint compares an equally lasting impact.
brief.meaningZh: 以足印比喻持久印象或影響；「較深」比較較強影響，「同樣深」比較相若的持久影響。
brief.grammar: leave a deeper footprint or leave the same deep footprint; left in past. Name the comparison and later evidence for stronger or equally lasting impact.
brief.register: Reflective figurative comparison; a reviewer or listener may tell a friend which work or moment stayed with them, while limiting the claim to the people compared.
brief.boundaryZh: 「較深」與「同樣深」的比較方向不同；兩者都須有持久記憶或影響的依據，不能單憑當下熱鬧程度或作品長短判斷。
brief.misconceptionZh: 當下較熱鬧或較長，不必然代表長遠影響較大。
brief.outcomeZh: 能以後續記憶或思考支持比較，保留個人感受範圍。

listening.en: The quiet conversation left a deeper footprint on my thinking than the opening spectacle: weeks later I was still reconsidering the question she had asked.
listening.zh: 安靜談話比開場盛大演出在我思考中留下更深足印：幾周後，我仍重新考慮她問的問題。
listening.promptZh: 甚麼支持 deeper 的比較？

options.en: The speaker was still thinking about the conversation weeks later.
options.zh: 幾周後說話者仍思考那段談話。

options.en: The opening spectacle was louder at the time, so it necessarily had the lasting effect.
options.zh: 開場當時較大聲，所以必定有持久影響。

options.en: An audience survey established that the whole group rated the conversation more highly.
options.zh: 觀眾調查確定整組對談話評價較高。

options.en: The speaker had forgotten both experiences before leaving.
options.zh: 說話者離開前已忘掉兩種體驗。

listening.explanationZh: 幾周後仍重新思考支持個人持久影響；不是只按當時聲量，亦未有整體調查或全忘記。

reply.promptZh: 你為甚麼說那段安靜談話的影響較深？
reply.promptEn: Why do you say the quiet conversation affected you more deeply?

options.en: I was still considering her question weeks afterwards.
options.zh: 幾周後我仍考慮她的問題。

options.en: It left a deeper footprint because her question kept shaping my thinking.
options.zh: 她的問題持續影響思考，所以留下更深足印。

options.en: The conversation remained important in my later reflection on the event.
options.zh: 談話在我後來對活動的反思中仍很重要。

options.en: My later reflection kept returning to what she had asked.
options.zh: 我之後反思時一直回到她問的事情。

reply.explanationZh: 四句給後續思考依據，不用音量或人人相同作判準。

scene.promptZh: 兩個故事在一個月後仍令你思考角色的選擇；你對兩者的記憶和後續討論相若，只想說自己的持久感受。哪句最準確？

options.en: Both stories left the same deep footprint on my thinking; a month later, I was still discussing each.
options.zh: 兩個故事在我的思考中留下同樣深的印象；一個月後我仍會談起兩者。

options.en: The first story left a deeper footprint than the second on my later thinking.
options.zh: 第一個故事在我之後的思考中留下比第二個更深的印象。

options.en: The stories made an impression that lasted only until the end of the reading session.
options.zh: 兩個故事的印象只維持到閱讀環節結束。

scene.explanationZh: 題目說兩個故事都有持久影響，而且後續記憶和討論相若；金句用 the same deep footprint 表示相若的持久影響，不能改稱第一個較深或兩者很快被忘掉。

contrast.promptZh: 哪項最不宜只憑 left a deeper footprint 得出？

options.en: The context describes a stronger lasting impression in a relevant comparison.
options.zh: 情境描述相關比較中較強的持久印象。

options.en: The audience as a whole has been shown to share the speaker’s preference.
options.zh: 已顯示整體觀眾都持有說話者的偏好。

options.en: The basis for deeper may be later memory or reflection.
options.zh: 較深的依據可來自之後的記憶或反思。

contrast.explanationZh: 個人持久印象不等於整體觀眾已調查同意。

dialogue.promptZh: 同伴想由你記得談話較久，推出開場演出對所有人都沒價值。哪句較準確？

options.en: The conversation left a deeper footprint on my thinking, but that reflects my experience, not the whole audience’s.
options.zh: 那段談話在我的思考中留下更深印象，但這只反映我的體驗，不能代表全體觀眾。

options.en: Use my memory as a record of how the whole audience responded.
options.zh: 把我的記憶當全體觀眾反應紀錄。

options.en: Could we use the opening’s greater loudness as the measure of the later impact instead?
options.zh: 我們可否改用開場較大聲作之後影響的尺度？

dialogue.explanationZh: 正確回答用目標比喻描述自己後續的思考，同時把比較限於個人經驗，不代全體觀眾，也不以當下音量代長期影響。

speaking.en: The exchange left a deeper footprint on my thinking than I expected.
speaking.zh: 那次交流在我思考中留下比預期更深的足印。
speaking.promptZh: 先聽，再描述自己的持續影響。

writing.promptZh: 新情境：你嘗試兩種學字方法，一次抄長字表、一次親自問路並用幾個詞，後來再訪該區仍記得問路用的字。你想寫自己的學習比較，下次再安排實際使用，不宣稱抄字對所有人無用。用一至兩句英文表達。
writing.selfCheckZh: 以再訪仍記得詞作個人比較依據，提出再使用計劃，不把自己的結果推成每人都只可用一種學習方式。

examples.en: Using the words to ask for directions left a deeper footprint in my memory than copying the long list. I want to practise using them again on my next visit.
examples.zh: 用詞問路比抄長字表在我記憶中留下更深足印。我想下次到訪再練習使用。

examples.en: The short exchange left a deeper footprint because I could still recall the words when I returned. I will build another real conversation into my practice.
examples.zh: 短交流留下更深足印，因回去時我仍記得那些詞。我會在練習中再安排一次真實對話。

takeaways.en: The small act of patience left a deeper footprint in her memory than the formal welcome.
takeaways.zh: 小小耐心行動比正式歡迎在她記憶中留下更深足印。

takeaways.en: The recorded story left the same deep footprint on both listeners; each still spoke of it years later.
takeaways.zh: 那段錄音故事在兩位聽眾心中留下同樣深的印象；多年後兩人仍會談起它。

brief.meaningEn: Developed gradually through successive additions or experiences, using a layered-construction image.
brief.meaningZh: 以層疊建構意象，形容透過接連累積而逐步形成。
brief.grammar: trust was built layer by layer; active build layer by layer; built is past and past participle; specify what each contribution adds.
brief.register: Natural figurative construction applied to understanding, trust or other gradual development. Not every use concerns a literal physical layer.
brief.boundaryZh: 逐層建立不保證每步都進步、結構永久穩固或已完成；需交代累積的內容。
brief.misconceptionZh: 一次行動可以是起點，不必等於整個關係或理解已建立。
brief.outcomeZh: 能描述連續貢獻如何累積，保留尚未完成及需維持的部分。

listening.en: Our understanding was built layer by layer: the first interview gave the outline, the diary added daily detail, and a later conversation helped us connect the two.
listening.zh: 我們的理解一層層建立：首次訪問給輪廓，日記加日常細節，後來談話幫我們把兩者連起來。
listening.promptZh: layer by layer 描述甚麼過程？

options.en: Successive sources added and connected parts of the understanding.
options.zh: 接連來源增添並連結理解的部分。

options.en: The first outline already contained every later detail.
options.zh: 首個輪廓已包含後來每項細節。

options.en: Each new source replaced the earlier one without using any of it.
options.zh: 每個新來源取代前一個，不用它任何內容。

options.en: The diary alone supplied the final account, with no contribution from either conversation.
options.zh: 只有日記提供最後敘述，兩次談話都沒有貢獻。

listening.explanationZh: 輪廓、日常細節及連結分次累積；不是首訪已全有、新來源全取代舊，或只靠日記。

reply.promptZh: 你們怎樣逐步了解那段經歷？
reply.promptEn: How did you gradually come to understand that experience?

options.en: The interview gave a start, then the diary and later conversation added detail and links.
options.zh: 訪問給起點，再由日記及後來談話加細節與連結。

options.en: Our understanding was built layer by layer from the different accounts.
options.zh: 我們從不同敘述一層層建立理解。

options.en: We connected the outline with daily details rather than relying on one source alone.
options.zh: 我們把輪廓與日常細節連起來，不只靠一個來源。

options.en: Each stage contributed something to the picture we were forming.
options.zh: 每個階段都為逐漸形成的整體增添內容。

reply.explanationZh: 四句都描述累積理解，不宣稱首訪已完整。

scene.promptZh: 社團新成員先學一項任務，再實際合作，之後按回饋調整，慢慢建立互信。哪句貼切？

options.en: Trust was built layer by layer through shared work and follow-up.
options.zh: 互信透過合作及跟進，一層層建立。

options.en: The introduction alone had already created enough trust for the newcomer to lead the next task without the shared practice.
options.zh: 單是介紹已建立足夠信任，讓新人不用共同練習就帶領下項任務。

options.en: Later feedback replaced the shared work rather than building on what members learned together.
options.zh: 後來回饋取代合作，而非建於成員一起學到的事。

scene.explanationZh: 先學、合作、回饋逐步增加互信；不是介紹已足夠帶任務，也不是回饋取代先前共同經驗。

contrast.promptZh: 哪項最不宜只憑 built layer by layer 得出？

options.en: Development involved successive contributions.
options.zh: 發展涉及接連貢獻。

options.en: The result is now permanently complete and cannot weaken.
options.zh: 結果現已永久完成，不會減弱。

options.en: The context should identify what was added over time.
options.zh: 情境應指出隨時間增加了甚麼。

contrast.explanationZh: 建構方式不保證永久、完全或毋須維持。

dialogue.promptZh: 同伴把首訪給的輪廓寫成已完整理解，但日記及後訪才補細節。哪句較準確？

options.en: Call the first interview a starting layer and show what the later sources added.
options.zh: 把首訪稱為起始一層，說明後來來源增加甚麼。

options.en: Then the first outline can serve as the final account, since the later sources only add background?
options.zh: 那首份輪廓可當最後敘述，因後來來源只加背景嗎？

options.en: Would it be better to treat the diary as a replacement for the interview rather than connect them?
options.zh: 是否把日記當訪問替代品，比連起兩者更好？

dialogue.explanationZh: 首訪給起點，日記加細節，後訪連起來；不能把起點當完整，也不把後來資料當只取代。

speaking.en: Our understanding was built layer by layer, and we still had questions to check.
speaking.zh: 我們的理解一層層建立，仍有問題待核對。
speaking.promptZh: 先聽，再把累積與尚待處理連起來。

writing.promptZh: 新情境：你寫一首小合奏，先定旋律，再加低音，最後試節奏；每次新增都要聽是否遮住原旋律，尚未定稿。用一至兩句英文描述編曲逐層形成及接下來的檢視。
writing.selfCheckZh: 交代旋律、低音、節奏的累積順序及每步聆聽檢視，不把新增當一定改善或已定稿。

examples.en: The arrangement was built layer by layer, from the melody to the bass and then the rhythm. I still need to check whether the added parts leave enough space for the tune.
examples.zh: 編曲由旋律到低音，再到節奏，一層層建立。我仍需檢查新增部分是否給旋律留足空間。

examples.en: I am building layer by layer rather than adding every part at once. After each addition, I listen for anything that covers the melody.
examples.zh: 我一層層建立，而非一次加所有聲部。每次新增後，我會聽有沒有遮住旋律的地方。

takeaways.en: Confidence was built layer by layer as the group practised and reflected on each attempt.
takeaways.zh: 小組練習並回顧每次嘗試時，信心一層層建立。

takeaways.en: The shared understanding had been built layer by layer, so we kept notes on how each part developed.
takeaways.zh: 共同理解一層層建立，所以我們記下各部分怎樣發展。
